install.command.title: Install command
install.command.failed: Select the text to copy it
install.command.note: Run the three lines together in the server’s root terminal. The first turns on clock synchronisation, because certificates need the right time. If the installation stops, run the same command again.

install.step.wizard: Sign in at the address the installer shows. The setup wizard asks for your domain and where DNS lives. A second server is optional.
home.title: CelikPanel · Hosting control panel for Debian and Ubuntu
home.description: A hosting control panel for Debian and Ubuntu servers: websites, mail, DNS, databases, certificates and backups. Your sites keep running with the panel or without it.
pricing.title: Pricing · CelikPanel
pricing.description: One price per server per year: 99 USD from version 1.0, with nothing counted and every feature. Free during the alpha.
pricing.hero.title: One price per server, per year.
pricing.hero.lede: Nothing counted, one edition. Free until 1.0.
pricing.included.title: Everything is included.
pricing.included.lede: No tiers, no add-ons. What the panel does, every licence does.
pricing.included.sites.name: Websites and applications
pricing.included.sites.text: PHP, Node.js and static sites, with the versions you choose, files and logs.
pricing.included.mail.name: Mail
pricing.included.mail.text: Mailboxes, forwarding, spam filtering, sending limits and webmail.
pricing.included.dns.name: DNS
pricing.included.dns.text: Your own name servers with BIND or PowerDNS, or an outside provider.
pricing.included.databases.name: Databases
pricing.included.databases.text: MariaDB and PostgreSQL, with users and exact rights.
pricing.included.security.name: Certificates and security
pricing.included.security.text: Free certificates, the firewall, security updates and the security emergency.
pricing.included.backups.name: Backups
pricing.included.backups.text: Scheduled site and server backups, restore and download.
pricing.included.people.name: Resellers and customers
pricing.included.people.text: Plans, rights and roles for everyone who works on the server.
pricing.included.pair.name: A second server, if you want
pricing.included.pair.text: Backup DNS on a second server. Each server has its own licence.
pricing.included.updates.name: Signed updates
pricing.included.updates.text: Started by you, with an automatic return to the previous version.
pricing.lapse.title: Nothing goes dark.
pricing.lapse.lede: Reminders, then thirty days with everything working. After that only new things wait.
pricing.terms.title: Try it, keep it, move it.
pricing.terms.lede: Written down before the first licence is sold.
pricing.terms.trial.text: Every feature for 30 days, without a card. Buying later keeps the same key.
pricing.terms.refund.text: Changed your mind within 30 days of buying? You get your money back.
pricing.terms.move.text: Move a licence to another server from your account, as often as you need. One active server per licence.
pricing.terms.auto: Automatic renewal only if you turn it on
pricing.terms.auto.text: With a reminder 7 days before every charge. It is never a side effect of something else.
pricing.terms.offline.text: Your panel keeps working fully for 30 days on its last successful check. One server’s licence never blocks another server.
pricing.terms.lifetime.text: Every licence is yearly, at the price you locked in when you bought it.
pricing.today.title: During the alpha.
pricing.today.free.text: Every licence is free and covers one server for one year from when you create it.
pricing.today.renew.text: Renewing is free, from your account.
pricing.today.check.text: The panel checks its licence about once an hour and keeps working for seven days without reaching celikpanel.net.
pricing.today.lock.text: Today almost every screen of the panel locks until the licence is renewed. Your sites, mail, DNS, databases and scheduled jobs keep running; they never ask for the licence.
pricing.today.founder.text: Beta participants get their first paid year free and a lasting founder price. The amount is not decided yet.
pricing.faq.title: Before you buy.
pricing.faq.stop.q: Does anything on my server stop when a licence ends?
pricing.faq.stop.a: No. Sites, mail, DNS, databases, backups, certificate renewal, updates and security keep working at every step. From version 1.0, after 30 days of grace only creating new domains, accounts and mailboxes waits for a renewal.
pricing.faq.server.a: One machine running the panel. A licence covers one active server at a time; if you add a second server, it has its own licence.
pricing.faq.count.q: Do I pay per account, domain or site?
pricing.faq.count.a: No. Nothing is counted. One licence per server covers everything on it.
pricing.faq.rise.a: Not while you renew without a break. The price you pay stays the price you pay.
pricing.faq.move.q: I am moving to a new server. What happens?
pricing.faq.move.a: From version 1.0 you move the licence to the new server yourself, from your account, for free, as often as you need.
pricing.faq.card.q: Do I need a card for the trial?
pricing.faq.card.a: No. The 30-day trial needs no card. Today, during the alpha, there is nothing to pay at all.
pricing.faq.service.q: What if your licence service cannot be reached?
pricing.faq.service.a: From version 1.0 the panel keeps working fully for 30 days on its last successful check; today that window is seven days. Your hosted services never depend on it.
pricing.faq.pay.a: Payment opens with version 1.0, in US dollars. The payment provider is not chosen yet.
download.title: Download and install · CelikPanel
download.description: Install CelikPanel with one command on a clean Debian or Ubuntu server: the signed release, the supported systems and how the panel changes your server.
download.hero.title: Install CelikPanel.
download.hero.lede: One command on a clean server. It downloads the signed release, checks it and installs the panel. No Go, Node.js or Git needed.
download.step.server: Prepare a clean server with one of the supported systems.
download.systems.title: Supported systems.
download.systems.lede: Tested: every release candidate runs on it first. Supported: it installs and runs.
download.systems.more: What each system offers, and how its updates work
download.wizard.title: The setup wizard finishes the job.
download.wizard.lede: On first sign-in it asks for your domain and where DNS lives. Each step says what it installs.
download.wizard.pair: A second server as backup DNS
download.wizard.pair.text: If you want one: a second server answers for your domains too, one main and one backup. You choose which is the main.
download.wizard.outside.text: No DNS software is installed. The panel lists the records to add and checks what the internet answers.
download.wizard.one.text: The usual start. The server keeps its own DNS, with both name server names on it.
download.wizard.two: Adding a second server, step by step
download.wizard.two.1: Install the panel on both servers, each with its own licence.
download.wizard.two.2: Go through the wizard on the first server. Choose mail on one server only.
download.wizard.two.3: When its setup starts, choose “Create a join code”. The code is shown once and is valid for 24 hours.
download.wizard.two.4: In the second server’s panel choose “Join the first server with a code” and enter the first server’s IP address and the code. The shared answers come from the first server.
download.wizard.two.5: With your own DNS, when the registrar card says so, set the name servers (NS) and their IP records (glue) at your domain registrar. The card checks them by itself.
download.how.title: How CelikPanel changes your server.
download.how.lede: One rule from railway signalling: once a route is set, every route that conflicts with it is locked.
download.how.preview.text: Before changing anything, the panel asks the server whether the change can be made. The answer is either a list of blockers or a single-use approval. If something blocks it, nothing changes.
download.how.commit.text: Only that approval makes the change. While it runs, the server holds one right to change; a second change waits its turn instead of stacking on top.
download.how.record.text: Every privileged change is written to a durable record with its outcome. If the power fails, the panel finds the unfinished work and finishes or reverses it; it never shows a half-done change as a success.
download.ledger.title: Measured, recorded, dated.
download.ledger.lede: Each value was measured on a real machine under the condition shown. They describe those tests, not a guarantee for every server.
download.ledger.restore.condition: The first server died in a power cut; the second was built from one sealed archive
download.ledger.age.condition: The archive’s real age at the moment of the cut; no record was lost
download.ledger.bind: Queries unanswered while adopting a running BIND
download.ledger.bind.condition: The server never stopped answering during the adoption
download.ledger.handbind.condition: Differences shown first, then adopted; again no query unanswered
download.ledger.power: Time to decide after a power cut
download.ledger.power.condition: Four cuts; each time the panel resolved the unfinished work with nobody touching the machine
download.ledger.accept.condition: Debian 13, Ubuntu 24.04 and Arch Linux: install, the database chain, restart
download.ledger.note: Test conditions, open risks and how each was closed are recorded in the repository.
download.trust.title: Signed, checked, yours to inspect.
download.trust.lede: You do not have to take the download on trust.
download.trust.signed: Every release package is signed. The installer checks the signature and the package checksum before it installs anything.
download.trust.notes: Every release’s notes name its commit and say what was tried in the lab, and what was not.
download.trust.split: The panel and its agent are two separate services. The web-facing panel runs without root; only the local agent may change the system.
download.trust.password: Your first administrator’s password is chosen on your server and is never sent to this website.
download.installed.title: Already installed?
download.installed.text: Update from inside your panel, under Settings, CelikPanel updates. Only you start it; nothing installs by itself.
systems.title: Supported systems · CelikPanel
systems.description: The Debian, Ubuntu and Arch Linux releases CelikPanel installs on: what is offered on each, what is not and why, and how updates work.
systems.hero.title: Supported operating systems.
systems.hero.lede: What is offered on each system, what is not and why, and how updates work.
systems.list.title: The list
systems.list.lede: Tested means every release candidate of CelikPanel runs on that system before it is published. Supported means CelikPanel installs and runs on it, but release candidates are not run on it. Dates are the distributions’ own support dates, checked on 24 October 2026.
systems.list.other: Other systems are not supported yet. Red Hat family systems (RHEL, AlmaLinux, Rocky Linux 9) are recognised, and the installer refuses them for now instead of half-installing. A system that is not on this list has not been checked. Linux amd64.
systems.table.caption: Operating systems CelikPanel supports
systems.updates.choice: Automatic or by hand, your choice
systems.arch.how: By hand, after reading the Arch news
systems.deb.title: Debian and Ubuntu
systems.deb.offered.text: All of CelikPanel’s components: web server and PHP, MariaDB and PostgreSQL, mail with Rspamd, DNS with BIND or PowerDNS, certificates, the firewall, backups and the security tools. Packages come from the distribution. Where a newer version is wanted, the panel offers a vendor repository only as a deliberate, confined, tracked choice.
systems.deb.notoffered.text: Apache, Exim and FTP (vsftpd) are not offered yet, on any system: their integration is not finished, so use Nginx and Postfix. Everything else in the catalogue is offered. Versions differ by release: for example Debian 13 ships PHP 8.4 and PostgreSQL 17, Ubuntu 24.04 ships PHP 8.3 and PostgreSQL 16. The panel shows what your release offers.
systems.deb.updates.text: Fixes come from the distribution’s security and update archives. The system’s own tool, unattended-upgrades, can install them every day by itself, or you install them by hand. You choose in the panel under Security, Security updates. The choice is one apt file on your server, so it keeps working while CelikPanel is stopped. If you edit that file yourself, the panel notices and asks before it replaces your text. The panel never restarts the server by itself.
systems.deb.major.text: A new major version of a program, such as PostgreSQL 17 after 16 or PHP 8.5 after 8.4, is a separate program and not an update. Updates fix the version you have. You move to a new major version yourself, when you decide.
systems.arch.offered.text: The server roles work with official Arch packages only: web, PHP, MariaDB, PostgreSQL, mail, certificates, the firewall and backups. PowerDNS comes from Arch’s extra repository as a first install. Valkey is offered where other systems offer Redis.
systems.arch.notoffered: What is not offered, and why
systems.arch.notoffered.1: phpPgAdmin and SpamAssassin: Arch’s official repositories carry no working package (only the AUR does, and CelikPanel does not use it). Manage PostgreSQL with psql, and use Rspamd as the spam filter.
systems.arch.notoffered.2: Redis: Arch ships the compatible Valkey instead, so Valkey is offered.
systems.arch.notoffered.3: Apache, Exim and FTP (vsftpd): not offered yet on any system. Use Nginx and Postfix.
systems.arch.notoffered.4: Switching an existing BIND server to PowerDNS: PowerDNS is offered as a first install only.
systems.arch.notoffered.5: Automatic upgrades: Arch has no security-only updates, and an unattended full upgrade can stop your services.
systems.arch.updates.text_html: Arch is a rolling release. An update is always a full upgrade that you run on the server: read archlinux.org/news first, then run sudo pacman -Syu, then check failed units, nginx -t, PHP-FPM and the mail services, and restart the server if the kernel changed. The panel counts what is waiting and shows these steps; it never runs the upgrade for you.
systems.arch.big.text: A full upgrade can move Arch’s php package to a new major version, and PostgreSQL to a new major version whose data directory must then be upgraded before the server starts again. Test your sites after the upgrade, or on a copy of the server first.
systems.yours.title: Your server stays yours.
systems.yours.text: CelikPanel operates your server; it does not own it. Sites, mail, DNS, databases, scheduled jobs and site certificate renewal keep running while the panel is stopped, on every system above.
systems.yours.detail: What is offered on which system, in detail
releases.title: Releases · CelikPanel
releases.description: The current CelikPanel release with its version, date, commit, SHA-256 and signed files, and how to check a download yourself.
releases.hero.title: Releases.
releases.hero.lede: Every release is signed and named by its commit. Installed panels update only when their owner starts it.
releases.check.title: Check a download yourself.
releases.check.lede: The installer does this before it installs anything. You can repeat it by hand.
releases.check.step1: Download the package, its SHA-256 file, the signed manifest, its signature and the public key into one folder.
releases.check.step2: Compare the key’s SHA-256 with the one printed below, then check the package against its SHA-256 file.
releases.check.step3: Verify the manifest’s signature with the key. The manifest names the package’s SHA-256 and size.
releases.check.key: SHA-256 of the release signing public key:
releases.check.note: Each line must end without an error: “OK” for the checksum, “Signature Verified Successfully” for the signature.
releases.update.title: Updating an installed panel.
releases.update.lede: Open Settings, CelikPanel updates, and press Check for updates. If the new version does not come up, the previous one returns.
releases.update.guide: How updates work, in the user guide

home.free.diagram: Diagram: when CelikPanel stops, websites, mail, DNS, databases, scheduled jobs and site certificate renewal keep running.
